props.title: ABSTRACT
props.subtitle: Both paths open at room temperature
props.note:
A porous host has two kinds of pore, wide channels and narrow side pockets, joined by openings. When CO_{2} is taken up, a single CO_{2} moves from one pore to the next through an opening. Here it is asked how a single CO_{2} moves, turns and tilts in the empty host, and what energy each motion costs.

For Path A, the barrier is 0.52 to 0.55 eV, whether the molecule turns before, during or after the move, or not at all.
For Path B, the barrier is 0.61 to 0.63 eV with the molecule turned to pass along its axis, and 1.40 eV when it passes broadside without turning.

Turning in place costs more in a narrow pocket than in a wide channel (0.30 to 0.45 eV against 0.04 to 0.06 eV). Paths that start with the molecule tilted 30° to 60° at the opening were also built, yet every one ends up passing along its axis, within 0.01 eV of the straight path.

Every barrier is found to fall as the host expands (0.08 to 0.12 eV per 1 % larger cell). Thus both openings are passed along the molecular axis, and Path B is found to cost 0.06 to 0.08 eV more than Path A.

An extra paragraph is added here so that the note runs past its line limit and the checker reports the overflow by line count, with the font size left unchanged.
